title: Quality of Advice Review (QAR) — Stage 2 Implementation
summary: Government progresses QAR recommendations to reduce the cost and complexity of personal advice, including simplifying SOA requirements and enabling more affordable scaled advice.
impactSummary: If enacted, SOA simplification could meaningfully reduce per-client compliance cost, improving advice economics and potentially expanding the addressable client base for advisers.

title: Compensation Scheme of Last Resort (CSLR) — Levy Structure Finalised
summary: ASIC has confirmed the annual levy structure for the CSLR, which requires licensees to fund compensation for clients of failed advice businesses. Levy amounts vary by adviser headcount.
impactSummary: Additional operating cost for licensees, particularly smaller AFS licensees. Could accelerate consolidation as compliance costs rise relative to revenue per adviser.

title: AFCA Membership — Expanded Jurisdiction for Advice Complaints
summary: AFCA's jurisdiction is expanded to include a broader range of financial advice complaints, with higher monetary limits for consumer remediation.
impactSummary: Higher potential liability exposure for licensees from expanded complaints jurisdiction. PI insurance costs likely to increase for practices with mixed-quality compliance histories.

title: Design and Distribution Obligations (DDO) — ASIC Enforcement Ramping Up
summary: ASIC announces increased surveillance of DDO compliance across product issuers and distributors, with specific focus on financial advice as a distribution channel.
impactSummary: Advisers must ensure product recommendations align with DDO target market determinations. Non-compliance risks licence conditions or banning orders.

title: FAAA CPD Year Requirements — 2024 Standards Updated
summary: The Financial Advice Association Australia updates its CPD year requirements, including minimum hours across ethics, technical competence, and professionalism categories.
impactSummary: Ongoing compliance requirement for all registered advisers. Adds time and cost but is now well-embedded in the advice profession.

title: Superannuation Performance Test — Advice Fund Implications
summary: APRA's annual superannuation performance test continues to affect MySuper and choice products. Funds that fail face restrictions on accepting new members.
impactSummary: Advisers recommending underperforming funds face increased scrutiny. Drives shift in super recommendations toward high-performing platforms and raises best-interest duty obligations.

title: ASIC Breach Reporting — Enhanced Obligations for Licensees
summary: Strengthened breach reporting obligations require licensees to report significant breaches within 30 days, with broader definitions of what constitutes a reportable situation.
impactSummary: Increased compliance overhead for licensees. Smaller licensees may struggle with the operational complexity of monitoring and reporting within prescribed timeframes.

title: Aged Care Advice — New Framework for Adviser Competency
summary: Government proposes new competency standards for advisers providing aged care financial advice, recognising the growing importance of this advice segment.
impactSummary: Could create a new specialist adviser category with additional qualification requirements. Opportunity for advisers who invest early in aged care competencies.

title: Financial Adviser Register — Enhanced Disclosure Requirements
summary: ASIC proposes enhanced public disclosure on the Financial Adviser Register including fee disclosure, complaint history, and product authority details.
impactSummary: Greater public transparency may drive client switching behaviour. Advisers with strong track records benefit; those with complaint history face increased reputational risk.

title: Life Insurance Framework (LIF) — Clawback Period Review
summary: Treasury initiates review of the LIF clawback provisions, following industry feedback that the two-year clawback period is discouraging risk advice provision.
impactSummary: Potential reduction in clawback risk could improve economics for risk insurance advisers. May arrest the decline in risk-focused advice practices.

title: Tax Agent Services Act — TASA Obligations for Financial Advisers
summary: ATO clarifies that advisers providing tax-related financial advice must comply with TASA obligations, including registration requirements and professional standards.
impactSummary: Advisers providing tax advice must ensure TASA registration or work through a registered tax agent arrangement. Adds compliance layer but clarifies the boundary between financial and tax advice.

title: ASIC Corporate Plan 2024–28 — Advice Market Supervision Priorities
summary: ASIC's four-year corporate plan identifies advice market quality and consumer protection as priority supervision areas, with increased surveillance of licensee compliance frameworks.
impactSummary: Signals continued regulatory scrutiny of advice quality. Licensees with weak compliance infrastructure should expect increased ASIC attention over the next four years.
